parole.significato: dragon's blood (Dracaena cinnabari, and other Dracaena species, and Calamus draco)
parole.testo: Anciently borrowed from Modern South Arabian, the three quality grades of dragon's blood being called in Soqotri for high quality ʔəmṣɔ́loh, medium quality ʔəʔī́daʕ, low quality fṣɔṣ, the tree ʔaʕarhī́yəb.

Unknown, with analogs only in Modern South Arabian – Mehri ديجر (dēdžer, dēdžir, dīdžer), Shehri دجرة (dəgərɛt), collective دجر (dúgur, dúger), Soqotri دنجة (déngoh), collective دجر (dégər, dígir) – and Cushitic – shown as descendants here assuming they agglutinated the Arabic article. Maybe metathe

Compare Soqotri [script needed] (lʼéḥim, léḥem, “shark”), Harsusi [script needed] (léḫem, “shark”), Mehri [script needed] (laḫáym, “shark”), which suggests a Modern South Arabian borrowing when Arabic expanded to South Arabia. A borrowing thence is anyhow likely in view of crosslinguistic comparison
